label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
The Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms (5-7 November 2026) wrapped up on Saturday at Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune. I was one of three organisers, and this post is on behalf of the team. It was student-run from start to finish.

A few numbers first, because they explain why the three days mattered to us. We received 112 applications for 41 seats. The 41 participants were MSc and early PhD students from 9 states, selected on the basis of a statement and one reference. A Rs 2.4 lakh student initiative grant from the institute covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation participants. That support made a real difference to who could attend.

Thank you to our speakers: Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad), who taught Mordell-Weil; Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai), who taught modular forms; and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki (Kraków), who joined online for computations in Sage. Each of them stayed for questions and made the material feel less intimidating. Thanks also to our faculty mentor, Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, and to my co-organisers, Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza. I should mention Mr. Prakash Salunke from the office, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11pm when the booking got messed up.

The six PhD student volunteers who did TA work deserve a special mention. They ran the problem sessions, and that format worked well. We should keep it.

Day 2 afternoon the power went for nearly two hours and laptops died. We moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. It ended up being the best session of the three days. In another session, an MSc student from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Sunanda ma'am's notes. She corrected it live and thanked him. Small schools like this matter more than big conferences for MSc students, because they get to actually ask questions.

Thank you to all the participants, who made the problem sessions worth running. We are grateful to everyone who came, asked questions, and stayed through the power cut.

Slides and problem sheets will go on the department website in two weeks. We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, depending on funding. Fingers crossed.
